recommendations.regimenLabel: Resuscitation + broad-spectrum antibiotics + anticoagulation (with urgent revascularisation)
steps: EMERGENCY — urgent CT angiography; do not delay for equivocal exam.
Resuscitate (fluids), broad-spectrum antibiotics, correct acidosis; NG decompression.
Urgent surgical/IR intervention — revascularisation (embolectomy/stent) and resect non-viable bowel.
Therapeutic anticoagulation for embolic/thrombotic arterial or venous occlusion.
ICU; high mortality — speed is critical.

drugRefs.dose: bolus 500 mL-1 L, then titrated to perfusion/urine output
drugRefs.why: Corrects the large third-space/volume losses and hypoperfusion; helps correct the metabolic acidosis.
Empiric Gram-negative/anaerobic cover for bacterial translocation across the ischaemic bowel wall; give early. Follow local antimicrobial policy.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Mesenteric Vascular Insufficiency
WSES Guidelines on Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia
ESVS Clinical Practice Guidelines — Mesenteric Ischaemia

drugRefs.dose: 80 units/kg bolus, then 18 units/kg/h infusion (titrate to APTT)
drugRefs.why: Therapeutic anticoagulation for embolic/thrombotic arterial or venous mesenteric occlusion; preferred peri-operatively for its short half-life and reversibility.

refs: WSES Guidelines on Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia
ESVS Clinical Practice Guidelines — Mesenteric Ischaemia

confirm: Severe abdominal pain OUT OF PROPORTION to exam, ± AF/vascular disease, rising lactate. CT angiography is key.
